newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap - Gas oil rebounds in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap - Gas oil rebounds in thin trade.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps rebounded from its overnight lows late afternoon on Thursday on some bargain hunting as the market corrected its early week big losess, traders said.
"The rebound is purely technical, there was some bargain hunting earlier in the day and prices moved up slightly," one trader said.
July paper was last quoted at $21.85/$21.95 per barrel, up from late Wednesday's $21.50/$21.70, brokers said.
August swaps also firmed which kept the July/August spread steady at minus 60 cents, they said. The July/August spread traded at this level earlier in the day.
August was last quoted up about 30 cents from Wednesday at $22.55/$22.70. August traded earlier in the day at $22.60 and $22.65, they said.

Traders said sentiment remained bearish due to the high stocks in Singapore with sellers lowering the floating differential to about 10-20 cents below spot quotes with some trades seen as low as minus 40 cents for prompt cargoes.
The high stocks were again seen from the latest stock data released by the Trade Development Board which showed a 339,000-barrel build to 11.575 million barrels for the week ended June 11.
The stock level is the highest in at least three years.
As a result of the prompt overhang, sellers have dropped their offers for early July cargoes sharply in order to entice buyers.
On Wednesday, a 150,000-barrel cargo for Jul 3-7 traded at $21.45 per barrel free-on-board compared to a trade at $22.20 on Monday.
The jet fuel/gas oil spread or regrade remained wide despite the rebound in gas oil prices.
The wide regrade was largely attributed to the plunge in gas oil prices with jet fuel holding relatively steady.
The July and August regrade was last quoted at $1.00/$1.30 per barrel with the bids seen able to improve further, brokers said. July regrade last traded at 75 cents early this week, they said.
Physical jet fuel traded at $23.00 per barrel free-on-board Singapore for Jul 3-7 lifting on Wednesday.

However, traders said the firmer jet fuel prices may be shortlived. This is because refiners have so far not switched operations to optimise jet fuel production but might be encouraged to do so in the wake of higher jet prices, which might in turn lead to higher stocks and lower prices.
Fuel oil swaps was last quoted down in part due to a weaker crude market with July last quoted at $98.50/$99.00 from $99.25/$99.75, brokers said.
Overnight August Brent crude closed down 31 cents to $17.77 per barrel on the International Petroleum Exchange and last traded unchanged.
